Been living here close to five years, and honestly, there's a lot to like about Hiranandani Regent Hill. The apartment itself is well-designed, they really maximized the space, which is great for a bhk. Security is top-notch, always see guards around, and that's a big plus for peace of mind. It's a gated community, which adds another layer of safety. I've found it to be a pretty quiet and serene place, especially considering it's in Powai. Plus, everything is close by a€“ shopping, dining, you name it. The gym is fully equipped, which is a big help for staying in shape. The staff are polite and decent, always willing to help. I have seen that hospitals are nearby, and cleanliness is appreciable. My wife loves the beautiful gardens, and D Mart being walkable is super convenient. Overall, it's a pleasant place to live.. Okay, so, it's not all sunshine and roses. Getting around can be a bit of a hassle. Autos aren't always readily available right outside the building, so you have to walk a bit. The washing machine that came with the apartment has been a pain, keeps overheating. Also, there's the issue of stray dogs, they seem to be everywhere, and the management doesn't seem to have much control over it. I've heard some single women say they don't feel entirely safe here, which is concerning. I have also noticed cockroaches all over the place. Finally, be careful about broker prices, they tend to hike them up.

I've been here a few years now, and honestly, it's a mixed bag. On the plus side, the location is fantastic. Powai is pretty central, and everything you need is close by. The apartment itself is well-furnished, and having AC and built-in cupboards in the bedrooms is a real bonus, especially for a smaller place. Plus, they've got a decent little park for the kids with swings, and it's nice seeing the elderly folks have a place to sit and chat. It's pretty clean around here, too, which I appreciate.. However, some things bother me. The management is super slow to address issues, which is frustrating. Also, the apartment size is definitely on the smaller side; my bedroom feels cramped. The basement parking is a mess, and honestly, the corridors sometimes smell like smoke. And the Airbnb situation is out of control; there are always new people coming and going, which makes it feel less like a community.

Well, I've been here at Hiranandani Regent Hill for, oh, must be four years now. And you know what? There's a lot to like. The location is just prime, everything's within walking distance a€“ the supermarkets, the restaurants, you name it. And being in Hiranandani, you get that nice, upscale feel, you know? Plus, the view of Powai Lake is something else, especially in the mornings. Security's pretty tight too, which gives you peace of mind. They've really made good use of the space, the apartments might be a bit compact, especially the 1 BHKs, but they're well-designed. And having a parking spot is a godsend in this city, let me tell you. I must say, having the D-Mart so close by is incredibly convenient for the daily needs.. Now, it ain't all sunshine and roses, mind you. The cleanliness can be a bit hit or miss sometimes, I've seen better. And while the apartments are well-designed, they can feel a bit cramped, especially if you've got a lot of stuff. The clubhouse is a bit of a letdown too, only the gym is really functional at the moment. And don't even get me started on the stray dogs, they can be a real nuisance, especially at night. Oh, and some of the pet rules seem a bit arbitrary, if you ask me. Also, I have heard from some other residents that they had a bad experience with the builder during the sales process.

I will say, the location of Hiranandani Regent Hill is pretty great, right in Powai. It's super convenient having everything nearby. The apartment itself is well-furnished, and the living area felt spacious, which is a plus. I appreciate that they provide a parking spot, too. The complex is clean and safe, and there's a park for the kids with swings, plus seating for older folks, which is nice to see.. Honestly, the management here can be a real pain. They don't seem to really address issues promptly. And while the location is great, the apartment itself is quite small, especially the bedroom a€“ barely any space! Storage is definitely limited. The basement parking is a mess, too. Plus, the corridors sometimes smell like smoke and alcohol, which is pretty gross.

Living in this society is none less than living in a seven star hotel. The society is known for the quality of construction and the amenities available. The society has a wonderful playground, sitting area, garden and a beautiful rooftop. Living here is pure luxury. The flats are spacious with good air circulation and natural lighting. There are good international schools nearby, along with the best healthcare facilities. All public transport is available easily. The area is also near to both western and eastern express highway. The airport is nearby too. There are many mufti- national companies and banks nearby. Everything that you ask for is available at your doorsteps like any food or groceries or other services. There are many entertainment centers like malls, quality restaurants and cinema halls nearby. There is an arrangement for power backup, the area is pet friendly and there is no problem of electricity or water supply. Parking facility is easily available. There are properly installed security cameras and there is frequent patrolling by police authorities making the area safe.. There are two major negatives of living here. The first one is that since the Mithi river is nearby, there is a problem of commuting specially during the monsoons, because of water logging. Due to the dumping ground nearby, the roads nearby smell terrible. Secondly, the slum area is situated just behind the society and thus due to this, there can problems like untidy environment, crowded market places and it is not advisable to travel late at nights since there have been a few cases of thefts. The resale value is less as the flats here are overly priced due to the good facilities available. Other than these, the area is just perfect and is one of the best.

This locality was planned and developed in 1964. Populated mainly with upper and middle- middle class sections of Maharashtrian, Konkani and South Indian communities with enclaves of East Indians and West coastal Catholic Christians. Mahim Kapad Bazar near Dargah is mainly Mohammedan. There are other communities also including pockets of Sindhis. All communities living in peaceful harmony. The broad Lady Jamshedji Road divides the area into almost two equal halves. Most buildings are G+3 built in late 1950s-early 1970s. Few new Towers have come up post redevelopment of some properties. This locality was planned and developed in 1964. Populated mainly with upper and middle- middle class sections of Maharashtrian, Konkani and South Indian communities with enclaves of East Indians and West coastal Catholic Christians. Mahim Kapad Bazar near Dargah is mainly Mohammedan. There are other communities also including pockets of Sindhis. All communities living in peaceful harmony. The broad Lady Jamshedji Road divides the area into almost two equal halves. Most buildings are G+3 built in late 1950s-early 1970s. Few new Towers have come up post redevelopment of some properties. There is City Light Market and Mahim Kapad Bazar Market which are well stocked with vegetables, seafood and meats. There is a thriving market of groceries and Provisions. There are several big shops selling everything from textiles, hardware, travel needs, and more. Bombay Scottish School is a top rung Coeducational ICSE School in the area. Additionally there is Victoria, Canossa, and St Michaels Schools all imparting quality English MH State Board Education. All state and private banks have their branches mainly on Lady Jamshedji Road. Hinduja Hospital is a leading healthcare services provider. There is Sitladevi Temple Campus, St Michaels Church, Victoria Church, the are British Raj era Maqdoom Mahimi Dargah, and Gurudwara. For leisure there is Paradise Cinema, the modern City Light Cinema, and the Star Theatres popularly called Badal-Bijlee theatres. Environment and public sanitation is clean all over the area. All daily necessity within walking distance. Excellent BEST Bus connectivity from Lady Jamshedji Road. Excellent train connectivity from Matunga Road station and Mahim Station to Western Railway and Central Railway Harbour Line. A short walk across Z Bridge over Matunga Station provides connection to Matunga Station on Central Railway Main Line. Dadar West is short distance away and Shivaji Park is within walking distance. All in all an excellent residential area to stay in high class locality with low monthly fixed living costs.

This locality was planned and developed in 1964. Populated mainly with upper and middle- middle class sections of Maharashtrian, Konkani and South Indian communities with enclaves of East Indians and West coastal Catholic Christians. Mahim Kapad Bazar near Dargah is mainly Mohammedan. There are other communities also including pockets of Sindhis. All communities living in peaceful harmony. The broad Lady Jamshedji Road divides the area into almost two equal halves. Most buildings are G+3 built in late 1950s-early 1970s. Few new Towers have come up post redevelopment of some properties. There is City Light Market and Mahim Kapad Bazar Market which are well stocked with vegetables, seafood and meats. There is a thriving market of groceries and Provisions. There are several big shops selling everything from textiles, hardware, travel needs, and more. Bombay Scottish School is a top rung Coeducational ICSE School in the area. Additionally there is Victoria, Canossa, and St Michaels Schools all imparting quality English MH State Board Education. All state and private banks have their branches mainly on Lady Jamshedji Road. Hinduja Hospital is a leading healthcare services provider. There is Sitladevi Temple Campus, St Michaels Church, Victoria Church, the are British Raj era Maqdoom Mahimi Dargah, and Gurudwara. For leisure there is Paradise Cinema, the modern City Light Cinema, and the Star Theatres popularly called Badal-Bijlee theatres. Environment and public sanitation is clean all over the area. All daily necessity within walking distance. Excellent BEST Bus connectivity from Lady Jamshedji Road. Excellent train connectivity from Matunga Road station and Mahim Station to Western Railway and Central Railway Harbour Line. A short walk across Z Bridge over Matunga Station provides connection to Matunga Station on Central Railway Main Line. Dadar West is short distance away and Shivaji Park is within walking distance. All in all an excellent residential area to stay in high class locality with low monthly fixed living costs.

Mumbai's Powai area is a vibrant and rapidly growing neighborhood that offers a perfect blend of urban convenience and natural beauty. Nestled around the picturesque Powai Lake, the locality boasts a scenic backdrop that adds charm. The well-planned area has excellent infrastructure, making it one of Mumbai's most sought-after residential and commercial hubs. Powai is known for its premium residential complexes, top-notch educational institutions like the Indian Institute of Technology IIT, and global corporate offices, making it an ideal location for professionals and families. The area also has a lively social scene with numerous cafés, restaurants and shopping centers, such as the popular Galeria Mall. Connectivity is another highlight, as Powai is well-connected to the rest of Mumbai via road and public transportation, including easy access to the Eastern and Western Express highways. Despite being in the city's heart, Powai retains a serene environment, with plenty of green spaces, parks and lakeside promenades perfect for leisure activities. Overall, Powai is a dynamic and well-rounded locality, offering a high standard of living with a mix of modern amenities and natural beauty. It is one of Mumbai's most desirable places to live and work.. Powai, though known for its scenic beauty and modern infrastructure, faces several challenges. Traffic congestion is a frequent problem, with narrow roads and ongoing construction causing regular jams, especially during peak hours. The cost of living is also notably high, with expensive real estate and daily expenses making it difficult for those on a budget. Waterlogging has become a growing concern as the area has seen a rapid influx of residents and corporate offices, resulting in parking shortages and crowded public spaces. The lack of direct public transportation, particularly no suburban railway access, forces residents to rely on buses and private vehicles, adding to travel time and costs. Additionally, waterlogging during the monsoon season is a persistent issue, affecting certain parts of the area and making commuting more difficult. While Powai remains a desirable neighborhood, these factors can be significant drawbacks for many.

Mumbai's Powai area is a vibrant and rapidly growing neighborhood that offers a perfect blend of urban convenience and natural beauty. Nestled around the picturesque Powai Lake, the locality boasts a scenic backdrop that adds charm. The well-planned area has excellent infrastructure, making it one of Mumbai's most sought-after residential and commercial hubs. Powai is known for its premium residential complexes, top-notch educational institutions like the Indian Institute of Technology IIT, and global corporate offices, making it an ideal location for professionals and families. The area also has a lively social scene with numerous cafés, restaurants and shopping centers, such as the popular Galeria Mall. Connectivity is another highlight, as Powai is well-connected to the rest of Mumbai via road and public transportation, including easy access to the Eastern and Western Express highways. Despite being in the city's heart, Powai retains a serene environment, with plenty of green spaces, parks and lakeside promenades perfect for leisure activities. Overall, Powai is a dynamic and well-rounded locality, offering a high standard of living with a mix of modern amenities and natural beauty. It is one of Mumbai's most desirable places to live and work.. Powai, though known for its scenic beauty and modern infrastructure, faces several challenges. Traffic congestion is a frequent problem, with narrow roads and ongoing construction causing regular jams, especially during peak hours. The cost of living is also notably high, with expensive real estate and daily expenses making it difficult for those on a budget. Waterlogging has become a growing concern as the area has seen a rapid influx of residents and corporate offices, resulting in parking shortages and crowded public spaces. The lack of direct public transportation, particularly no suburban railway access, forces residents to rely on buses and private vehicles, adding to travel time and costs. Additionally, waterlogging during the monsoon season is a persistent issue, affecting certain parts of the area and making commuting more difficult. While Powai remains a desirable neighborhood, these factors can be significant drawbacks for many.

Mumbai's Powai area is a vibrant and rapidly growing neighborhood that offers a perfect blend of urban convenience and natural beauty. Nestled around the picturesque Powai Lake, the locality boasts a scenic backdrop that adds charm. The well-planned area has excellent infrastructure, making it one of Mumbai's most sought-after residential and commercial hubs. Powai is known for its premium residential complexes, top-notch educational institutions like the Indian Institute of Technology IIT, and global corporate offices, making it an ideal location for professionals and families. The area also has a lively social scene with numerous cafés, restaurants and shopping centers, such as the popular Galeria Mall. Connectivity is another highlight, as Powai is well-connected to the rest of Mumbai via road and public transportation, including easy access to the Eastern and Western Express highways. Despite being in the city's heart, Powai retains a serene environment, with plenty of green spaces, parks and lakeside promenades perfect for leisure activities. Overall, Powai is a dynamic and well-rounded locality, offering a high standard of living with a mix of modern amenities and natural beauty. It is one of Mumbai's most desirable places to live and work.. Powai, though known for its scenic beauty and modern infrastructure, faces several challenges. Traffic congestion is a frequent problem, with narrow roads and ongoing construction causing regular jams, especially during peak hours. The cost of living is also notably high, with expensive real estate and daily expenses making it difficult for those on a budget. Waterlogging has become a growing concern as the area has seen a rapid influx of residents and corporate offices, resulting in parking shortages and crowded public spaces. The lack of direct public transportation, particularly no suburban railway access, forces residents to rely on buses and private vehicles, adding to travel time and costs. Additionally, waterlogging during the monsoon season is a persistent issue, affecting certain parts of the area and making commuting more difficult. While Powai remains a desirable neighborhood, these factors can be significant drawbacks for many.

Mumbai's Powai area is a vibrant and rapidly growing neighborhood that offers a perfect blend of urban convenience and natural beauty. Nestled around the picturesque Powai Lake, the locality boasts a scenic backdrop that adds charm. The well-planned area has excellent infrastructure, making it one of Mumbai's most sought-after residential and commercial hubs. Powai is known for its premium residential complexes, top-notch educational institutions like the Indian Institute of Technology IIT, and global corporate offices, making it an ideal location for professionals and families. The area also has a lively social scene with numerous cafés, restaurants and shopping centers, such as the popular Galeria Mall. Connectivity is another highlight, as Powai is well-connected to the rest of Mumbai via road and public transportation, including easy access to the Eastern and Western Express highways. Despite being in the city's heart, Powai retains a serene environment, with plenty of green spaces, parks and lakeside promenades perfect for leisure activities. Overall, Powai is a dynamic and well-rounded locality, offering a high standard of living with a mix of modern amenities and natural beauty. It is one of Mumbai's most desirable places to live and work.. Powai, though known for its scenic beauty and modern infrastructure, faces several challenges. Traffic congestion is a frequent problem, with narrow roads and ongoing construction causing regular jams, especially during peak hours. The cost of living is also notably high, with expensive real estate and daily expenses making it difficult for those on a budget. Waterlogging has become a growing concern as the area has seen a rapid influx of residents and corporate offices, resulting in parking shortages and crowded public spaces. The lack of direct public transportation, particularly no suburban railway access, forces residents to rely on buses and private vehicles, adding to travel time and costs. Additionally, waterlogging during the monsoon season is a persistent issue, affecting certain parts of the area and making commuting more difficult. While Powai remains a desirable neighborhood, these factors can be significant drawbacks for many.

Sher e punjab colony in Andheri east, Mumbai is a locality inhabited by people from different communities, backgrounds and this diversity makes it a perfect for living. The pleasant living conditions and easy access to different parts of the city with its outskirts attract many new residents with trendy lifestyle. Nestled along the foothills of the famous Sanjay Gandhi National Park, the locality has great access to the Eastern Express Highway and Navi Mumbai via the Mulund-Airoli Bridge.. Mulund Station falls on the central line of Mumbai railway. Mulund is not well connected to other suburbs and other cities as well by adequate network of trains, BEST buses and roads including a national highway. Mulund is a stop for slow local trains as well as semi-fast local trains on the central line of the Mumbai suburban network. Alright, so I've been living here at Sunteck City for almost two years now. Gotta say, the location is pretty convenient. You got your Ram Mandir Railway Station, Dmart, and SV Road all nearby, which is a blessing. The apartment itself is spacious and well-designed, and I must admit, the interior of these blocks has a classy, modern touch. The guards are also very cooperative and vigilant, which makes you feel safe. Plus, having 24 hours water supply is a big relief. They do have a play area for the grandads when they visit, and it's a pretty lively place, I must say. Essential items are available within half a kilometer, so that's handy too. And the parking structure is pretty good, no complaints there.. There are some issues that bother me. For starters, the amenities, they're only for namesake, really. And there's this persistent rat smell in the society, which is quite unpleasant. Living here can be highly inconvenient at times, and there are leakages every now and then, which leads to dampness in the walls. I even saw some wall tiles literally fall off! And don't even get me started on that narrow lane; driving out is a nightmare. Plus, they promised a multipurpose play area, but it's been a year since possession, and still nothing. It's quite disappointing, to be honest.

The location of Sunteck City is amazing, especially with the Western Express Highway being so close. Getting around is super easy, and everything's pretty accessible. I also feel pretty safe with the security cameras and smoke detectors in every room. Plus, they have so many pools and play areas, and even a football field! It's really nice to have those options.. The apartment itself doesn't quite match the outside. The construction quality is not that good. The gym is way too small for the number of people living here. It's inconvenient. There's still some construction going on, which is a bit annoying, and honestly, the service could be way better. It's just not what I expected, especially considering the price.

I gotta say, living here has its perks. The location is pretty sweet, being close to the highway connected bridge makes getting around much easier. Plus, the amenities are well-maintained, I mean, having a swimming pool, gym, walking track, and even a carrot room and pool table is pretty awesome. The community vibe is great too; people are always celebrating events together, which is nice. The apartment sizes are decent, and there's usually a great breeze flowing through.. On the other hand, there are some real downsides. The parking situation is a complete mess, badly planned from the start. The construction quality is questionable; most walls seem to be made of plaster, and there are leakage issues in some flats. I've also heard neighbors complaining about the flats being pigeon holes. And don't even get me started on the gas situation a€“ there's no gas pipeline, so we're stuck buying cylinders. Also, the kids complain about the playground space, its too small for them.

Okay, so, the location is pretty convenient, right next to Dmart and a short walk to Ram Mandir station, which is a big plus for getting around. They do have some nice amenities, like a garden and a basketball area, and the clubhouse is kinda fancy, reminds me of Bombay Gymkhana. The security seems on top of things, which is always reassuring. Plus, parking is available for both residents and visitors, and the lifts are automatic, which is nice. The top west-facing flats have a great view, I've heard.. Man, where do I even start? The construction quality is seriously questionable. I've seen leakage issues in the washrooms and cracks all over the walls. The rooms are surprisingly small for such a high-end project. And don't even get me started on the stack parking a€“ it's practically unusable and not what we agreed on. The locality itself isn't great, and the builder backtracked on the Mahanagar Gas Pipeline. You can't even park two cars at a time because of the height restrictions. The wooden frames are also a concern.

Well, I've been at Godrej Central for about a year and a half now, and I must say, it's been quite pleasant. The community here is truly special a€“ feels like one big family, with always something happening. It's a safe and peaceful place, especially if you're seeking a quiet family environment. Connectivity is excellent; getting to EEH, BKC, and other parts of Mumbai is easy. They offer all kinds of amenities a€“ badminton, a gym, and a garden for the kids. Plus, everything is nearby a€“ medical stores, grocery stores, even a vegetable market. Can't complain about that! It's a lively, cosmopolitan society mainly full of professionals, so it's not too noisy either. They even have a turf area and a skating rink! Honestly, I wouldn't want to be anywhere else.. Now, I don't usually complain, but if I had to nitpick, I'd say the society management could be a bit more responsive sometimes. And while the construction seems solid enough, I've noticed a few minor issues here and there that could use some attention. But honestly, these are just small things, and overall, it's a great place to live.

I've been living here for about a year and a half, and honestly, it's been pretty good. I really appreciate how secure the complex is; they've got a first-class security system, and having security cameras on the door gives me extra peace of mind. Plus, it's so convenient being close to the railway station and metros a€“ getting around Mumbai is surprisingly easy, even with traffic. It's a very nice place, centrally located. The community is vibrant, and it's great seeing so many families and senior citizens feeling safe and comfortable. The amenities are a nice bonus, especially the walking path and recreation center. I also like that the layout is thoughtfully planned.. Honestly, I don't really have any major complaints. Sometimes the parking can get a little crowded, but that's about it. It would be great if they had a bit more space for visitors to park. Also, the maintenance could be a little bit more proactive.

Sometimes it gets a little noisy during festivals, but it's all in good fun.

If I had to nitpick, maybe more could be done to improve traffic flow around the entrance during peak hours. And while the cultural activities are great, sometimes they can get a bit noisy if you're trying to relax at home. But overall, these are minor issues compared to the benefits of living here.

Plus, it's so convenient being close to the railway station and metros a€“ getting around Mumbai is surprisingly easy, even with traffic. It's a very nice place, centrally located. The community is vibrant, and it's great seeing so many families and senior citizens feeling safe and comfortable. The amenities are a nice bonus, especially the walking path and recreation center. I also like that the layout is thoughtfully planned.. Honestly, I don't really have any major complaints. Sometimes the parking can get a little crowded, but that's about it. It would be great if they had a bit more space for visitors to park. Also, the maintenance could be a little bit more proactive.

Living here has been pretty good for the family. The kids are always busy with something, whether it's the rock climbing thing they have or just running around with the other kids. It's a relief knowing they're safe with the CCTV everywhere. The management actually seems to care, which is a nice change from other places I've lived. We've really enjoyed all the festivals; the community really gets into it. I use the gym regularly, and it's decent enough. Plus, having the badminton and table tennis is great for a quick workout. It's nice being able to walk to the market and even the train. It's like a little oasis amidst the Mumbai chaos, I must say. Everyone is so helpful here, and the community is very vibrant.. Honestly, I don't have any major complaints. Maybe the parking situation could be better, but that's a common problem everywhere, isn't it? Sometimes it gets a little noisy during festivals, but it's all in good fun.

Been living here almost two years now, and I gotta say, the location is a huge win. Being smack-dab in the center of things makes getting to work super easy, especially with all the office areas nearby. It's really convenient for professionals and feels safe for families too. Plus, the airport's not too far, which is a lifesaver for travel. The neighbors are genuinely helpful, and there's a real sense of community. The society itself is well-maintained and clean, which is a big plus. It's also surprisingly spacious considering how crowded Chembur and Tilak Nagar can be. They've got a great cultural committee that organizes lots of activities, and having a gym and even a skating rink is pretty cool. It's a cosmopolitan vibe with pretty much everything you need within walking distance.. Honestly, it's hard to find major faults. If I had to nitpick, maybe more could be done to improve traffic flow around the entrance during peak hours. And while the cultural activities are great, sometimes they can get a bit noisy if you're trying to relax at home. But overall, these are minor issues compared to the benefits of living here.

I've been here for about a year now, and honestly, it's grown on me. The best part is how easy it is to get around Mumbai from here. Plus, it's close to a lot of office areas, which makes the commute a breeze. It feels safe and peaceful, and the people around here are really good. The place is well-maintained and neat and clean, and they've got 24-hour water, which is a big relief. There's even a skating rink, which is cool. It's a multi-tower gated community, and there's a really amazing vibe here. You really won't want to be anywhere else.. If I had to nitpick, I'd say that sometimes the recreation center can get a little crowded, especially on weekends. Also, it would be nice if they had even more green spaces.

Godrej Central, it's been quite lovely. The location is just superb! Being so close to the railway station and metros makes getting around so easy, especially when visiting my grandads. Well, I've been calling Hiranandani Highland home for almost three years now, and I must say, it's been quite the experience. The location is just superb; you're right in the heart of things with easy access to all the major roads and transportation. It's so convenient! And the view? Absolutely stunning, especially at night with the city skyline all lit up. They've got a pool which is nice for a dip in the summer, and having a D-Mart right nearby is a godsend for us old folks. Plus, you're close to some really good restaurants if you don't feel like cooking. The building itself is top-notch, with great amenities like pipe gas, and the architecture is remarkable. It's a relaxed housing facility, and the luxurious interiors really make it feel like home.. Now, I wouldn't say everything is perfect, mind you. Sometimes, the lift can be a bit slow, especially during peak hours, which can be a bit frustrating. And while the society tries their best to maintain everything, there are times when things could be a bit cleaner, especially around the common areas. Also, the parking situation can be a bit tight sometimes, especially when there are visitors. But overall, these are just minor inconveniences, nothing too serious.

I've been living here for almost three years, and honestly, the best part is how safe I feel. They've got round-the-clock security, and the staff is really dedicated. The building itself feels premium, and I appreciate the little things like the elegant foyer. Having two parking spots is a huge plus, and the internet is super reliable, which is essential for my work. Also, a refrigerator is provided which is great. It really does give a distinctive living experience that caters to those who demand nothing but the best. I enjoy walking on the pavements in the evenings.. It's tough to find major faults, but if I had to nitpick, I'd say the society could use a bit more in terms of visitor parking. Sometimes, it's a hassle for my friends to find a spot when they come over. Also, while the construction is good, the electricity bills can be a little high, which is something to keep in mind.

Living here these past couple years, the thing that really stands out is how close we are to my office. Makes the commute a breeze, which is a huge plus. And I have to say, that rooftop infinity pool? It's a true gem. I often head up there for a refreshing escape after a long day. The architecture is also pretty impressive; it's a modern building, but it doesn't feel cold or sterile. Inside, the kitchens and bathrooms are thoughtfully designed, which my wife appreciates. Plus, having 24-hour water is something you don't realize is a luxury until you've lived somewhere without it. Also, the concierge service is a nice touch, makes life a little easier. Good schools nearby is a relief since my elder one is about to start schooling. Roads are wide and well maintained, which helps a lot.. Honestly, it's hard to complain too much, but if I had to pick something, it's that it can feel a little disconnected from the rest of the city sometimes. While being near the office is great, getting anywhere else can take a while.

Living here has been pretty good overall. The fitness center is a real plus, I've been using it regularly and it's got all the latest equipment. The views are amazing, especially from the higher floors a€“ you can see for miles. I like that there aren't any slums nearby; it keeps the area clean and safe. The apartments themselves have really nice finishes and the layouts are spacious, with plenty of natural light. Plus, it's nice not having street vendors everywhere.. Groceries, services, you name it a€“ it's all a little pricier. While they advertise the AC rooms, it's more of a standard feature these days, so it's not a selling point. Also, while the place is generally serene, that comes at a cost, and you end up paying a premium for it.

I gotta say, the open spaces at Kalpataru Radiance are a major plus. It really does feel like a little escape from the city. I've had some really great experiences just walking around, and the architecture is pretty impressive. They've got a spa and fitness center, which is great for unwinding after work. The staff seems pretty professional too, always ready to help.. There are a few things that bother me. They're still using COVID as an excuse for some delays, which is annoying. And while the park is nice, it's actually owned by TMC, not the society. Plus, people from outside the complex use our roads for dog walks, and it's not always pretty. I'm also a bit worried about the construction quality after hearing some neighbors talking, and the security isn't quite as tight as they advertised. Also, the main door frame seems pretty weak.

I've been living in Kalpataru Radiance for a year now, and there are definitely some things I like. The greenery is a big plus; there are lots of landscaped gardens and open spaces. I also appreciate the amenities, like the clubhouse, pool, and gym. It's nice to have those options right here. And the Grand Central Park is a great addition.. The construction quality could be better. I've noticed some potholes on the roads, and the main entrance road is starting to deteriorate. Also, I'm a bit concerned about security; the main entrance is often unmanned, and it doesn't seem like they're interested in increasing security measures. It's also been quite a hassle to get issues resolved with the management. It has ruined my peace of mind.

The society is pretty spacious, and they've done a good job with the layout. The security is tight, which gives you a sense of safety, especially for the grandads when they visit. Not exactly next door.

Living in Lodha Raj Infinia definitely has its perks. I mean, the location is amazing a€“ you've got Infinity Mall, the Metro, and Link Road all super close, which makes getting around and finding stuff to do really easy. MovieTime and all the restaurants nearby are a huge plus when you don't feel like cooking. Plus, the building itself has some pretty sweet amenities. The gym is well-equipped, and I like having the indoor games area and the garden to chill in. Steam and sauna are a bonus. Overall, it delivers pretty well on the luxury front.. Okay, so here's the thing. While the location and amenities are great, the building has had its share of issues. Honestly, there was a period where it felt like nothing was getting done, and the building felt like it was rotting. I'm also a bit worried about potential leakage in the flats down the line, given some of the stuff I've seen. And I wish the communication from the management was better; it's often hard to get updates on ongoing work or address concerns effectively. It feels like they are not transparent about what is going on.

Overall, it is worth investing here in the right society.

The society here are very safe and secure. There are security guards and cameras installed at the necessary locations. Most of the societies here are gated. Frequent police patrolling is done at nights and the area is safe for women and children. There are many good schools and colleges nearby. A number of good hospitals and banks are nearby. Markets are situated at a walkable distance and all essentials and groceries are available at a walking distance. There is good public transportation available. The connectivity of buses and private taxis is good. Railway station is also nearby and the area is well connected to all parts of Mumbai. Metro railway is also nearby. The airport is also just twenty minutes away. No power shortages have been experienced lately. Power backup facility is also available. There is twenty four hours supply of water. There are a number of malls, multiplexes and restaurants in the neighborhood. Most of the societies have good lift facility, indoor gyms and swimming pool.. There are many issues related to parking space for visitors. It is very difficult to find even a paid parking spot. A few cases of car thefts have also been reported. The condition of the roads is bad and potholes, cracked surfaces are also a common issue. There is a lot of traffic during the peak hours. It is very troublesome during the rains and peak hours. There are a number of street vendors who encroach the area after evenings and this has led to a lot of mosquitoes and street dogs in the area, crowding at night and unhygienic environment. There are very few parks in the area. Most of them are not well maintained. Hence the quality of air is not clean and fresh. It becomes a bit difficult to find shared autos and taxis during nights. Fire extinguishers need to be made available in all the societies. In general, there are many good societies here, however their maintenance charges are a bit high due to the location advantage. Overall, it is worth investing here in the right society.

Living here, the best part is definitely the view. I mean, waking up and seeing the race course and the sea, it's pretty special. Living at Piramal Mahalaxmi for a year now, and must say, the views are something' special. That sea view, especially at sunrise and sunset, just takes your breath away. The location is good in South Mumbai, which makes getting around fairly easy. The apartments are designed in such a way that you get a lot of privacy, only four residences on each floor, which is a big plus. And those show flats? Beautifully done, gives you a real sense of what it's like to live here. They even showed us marble samples, which was a nice touch.. Now, it's not all perfect, mind you. With all the upcoming development on the Mahalaxmi racecourse, I'm a bit worried about how crowded it might get. And while the project is magnificent, I've heard whispers that 'they're backing out' from some folks, which is a bit concerning, though I haven't seen any concrete evidence myself. It could also use a bit more green space; it sometimes feels too concrete. Also, the pool and landscape are nice, but could be better maintained.

I gotta say, the views here at Piramal Mahalaxmi are seriously something else. Waking up and seeing the racecourse and the Arabian Sea is pretty amazing. Plus, the building itself is super luxurious and it's in a great location. I've been living here for a year now, and I think it's definitely a landmark building. The infinity pool is awesome too!. One thing that's been bugging me, though, is that they promised us flooring selection options, but then they went back on their word. That's pretty disappointing coming from a brand like Piramal. Also, while it's the largest residential project in South Mumbai, it can feel a bit crowded sometimes.

There are also no good neighbors. Because of this, I disliked this society. Additionally, it is an expensive place.

Piramal Mahalaxmi, while impressive in luxury offerings and panoramic views, comes with a few drawbacks. Runwal Greens is a premium residential complex located in Mulund West, a prominent locality in Mumbai's suburbs. Here are some positive things about Runwal Greens: Prime Location: Runwal Greens is located in a prime location in Mulund West, with easy access to major highways, railway stations, and airports. The complex is just 10 minutes away from the Mulund railway station and 30 minutes away from the Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport, making it a convenient location for commuters. Luxurious Amenities: Runwal Greens offers a range of luxurious amenities such as a clubhouse, swimming pool, gymnasium, indoor games room, kids' play area, and landscaped gardens. The complex also has a multipurpose hall, tennis court, basketball court, and squash court, providing residents with a variety of options for recreation and entertainment. Well-Designed Apartments: The apartments in Runwal Greens are well-designed and spacious, with modern amenities and fittings. The complex offers 2, 3, and 4 BHK apartments, ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 square feet in size. Well-Maintained: The complex is well-maintained with 24x7 security and surveillance, ensuring a safe and secure living environment for residents. The maintenance staff is available round the clock to address any issues that residents may face. Green Surroundings: Runwal Greens is surrounded by lush greenery, with landscaped gardens and open spaces. The complex is designed to provide a serene and peaceful living environment away from the hustle and bustle of the city. Overall, Runwal Greens offers a luxurious and comfortable living experience in a prime location in Mumbai.. While Runwal Greens in Mulund West has many positive aspects, there are also some potential negative aspects that should be considered. Here are some of them: High Price: Runwal Greens is a premium residential complex, and the prices of the apartments are relatively high compared to other residential complexes in the area. This may make it unaffordable for some people. Crowded: Runwal Greens is a large residential complex with several buildings, which means that it can get crowded at times. This can result in congestion in common areas such as the clubhouse and swimming pool, especially during peak hours. Noise Pollution: Mulund West is a busy area with heavy traffic, which can result in high levels of noise pollution. Residents of Runwal Greens may experience some amount of noise pollution, especially if their apartment faces the main road. Distance from the City Center: While Mulund West is well-connected to the rest of Mumbai, it is located at a distance from the city center. This may make it inconvenient for those who have to travel to the city center frequently for work or other purposes. Limited Parking Space: Runwal Greens provides limited parking space for residents, which may be a concern for those who own multiple vehicles. Additionally, parking may be difficult to find during peak hours or special events.

Well, I must say, Ruparel Jewel has been quite alright for the past couple of years. The location, you see, is a real boon. All in all, it's a pretty good place to be.. Construction, while solid enough, isn't exactly top-notch. I've seen better, I must say. And while they boast about all the amenities, some of them feel a bit€¦ incomplete, if you catch my drift. Plus, sometimes it feels a bit isolated, like we're in the middle of nowhere. And property value? Well, let's just say I'm not entirely convinced it's going to skyrocket like they promised. Still, it's not all bad, just a few things that could be better.

Ruparel Jewel is definitely on the high-end side. The apartments are pretty spacious and feel airy, which I really appreciate. The view from the wrap-around deck is amazing, especially at night. The amenities are pretty good too, I use the gym regularly.. It feels like it's in the middle of nowhere sometimes, especially if you're trying to get a cab late at night. And I've heard from some other residents that there hasn't been much progress on some of the construction lately. I also wish there was more green space, it's kinda lacking in that department. Also, while they respond to queries, it sometimes takes them a while to actually fix things.

I gotta say, the apartments at Ruparel Jewel are fabulous, no doubt. We've got one of the bhk, and the views from the with floor are spectacular, especially the sea view. Living in Rustomjee is a delightful experience, nestled in the most prestigious neighborhoods. Feeling of luxury. All basic amenities are near by like hospitals and schools. Modern architecture with spacious rooms and a proper safety for residents.. What I dislike most is the ongoing construction work around our building. Elevators are crowded during the peak evening hours. Parking spaces are in short supply. The high price of this building, and traffic during the peak rush hours are the main problems.

Alright, so I've been calling Rustomjee Crown home for about two years now, and honestly, there's a lot to like. They really push that 'high standards of community living' thing, and you know what? They mostly deliver. I do love my apartment, especially being up on one of the top floors a€“ feels like you're living in the clouds, with that sea view. The amenities are pretty good too, keeps the grandads entertained when they visit. The staff is usually courteous and helpful, always attending to our needs, which is a big plus for us old timers.. We've had a few issues that have been quite bothersome. I hate to say it, but some neighbors have complained about rats, which is just unacceptable in a 'luxury' complex like this. There has been some discussion about the sprinklers not being ready in the event of a fire, which is a genuine safety concern. Additionally, I've heard whispers about water damage being a common issue, which worries me about the long-term construction quality. These issues need to be addressed, or it significantly detracts from the overall experience.

Living at Rustomjee Crown has its perks, I will admit. The location is truly superb, right in the center of everything, which makes getting around super easy. The grand lobbies really do give a sense of luxury every time I come home. I enjoy having access to the table tennis, and the walking track is a nice touch for getting some exercise. Plus, the maintenance team generally keeps things in good shape, which is a big relief. The idea of living so high up, in one of those 68-story towers, is pretty cool, I can't lie. And the green spaces, while maybe not huge, are a welcome sight in the city.. The construction noise is a major issue. Seriously, the loud drilling goes on almost 24/7, which is incredibly disruptive, especially when you're trying to work from home or just relax. Also, I've had some serious problems with my apartment not getting finished properly a€“ it's been two months, and things are still incomplete. And the ACs breaking down? That's just unacceptable, especially considering how much we pay to live here. For a 'quality construction,' there sure are a lot of ongoing issues.

Living here at Rustomjee Crown for over two years, I gotta say, the views are something else. We're on a higher floor, facing east, and waking up to that Mumbai skyline is pretty special. They call these apartments 'assets,' and honestly, with the way property prices are going, they might be right! The complex itself is well-maintained, and the amenities are a big plus – the gym is decent, and the kids practically live in the swimming pool. Parking's never really been an issue for us, which is a relief. Security seems pretty tight, too, which gives the wife peace of mind.. That being said, it's not all sunshine and roses. I'm a bit worried about some safety measures. It's the small things, you know? Like when we first moved in, the smoke detectors were still covered in plastic! Makes you wonder what else they missed. And honestly, dealing with management can be a real headache.

I've been living here for almost two years, and there's a lot to like. The construction quality seems very solid, and the amenities are definitely a highlight. They've got a café that's really convenient, and the kids' area is a big plus for families. The banquet facilities are also quite nice. I'm looking forward to when all the planned amenities are fully operational because they sound amazing. The views are quite good from my apartment too.. The biggest issue right now is the ongoing construction. There's dust everywhere, and it's often a complete mess. Honestly, the management, which is handled by Ruastomjee's internal team, Crest, hasn't been great. They're slow to address issues, and things feel a bit disorganized. It feels like they're still figuring things out, and it impacts the overall living experience.

The construction quality at Rustomjee Crown is truly impressive, exuding luxury and thoughtful planning. The amenities are top-notch, and the views from the top floors are absolutely breathtaking. I'm quite disappointed with the management's focus, as my flat hasn’t seen any maintenance in over two months. The delivery timeline seems to be an issue, especially with Tower B being neglected while they prioritize Tower C.

The construction quality is excellent. The location near the Parel and Prabhadevi stations is very convenient. The luxurious homes and stunning views are truly impressive. Their rules are absurd, and they need to change them before someone gets irritated.

Well, after living here at Godrej Nest for almost seven years, I can say it's a mixed bag. On the bright side, the security is very nice, makes you feel safe, you know? And the place is huge, plenty of space for the grandads to run around when they visit. The units themselves are quite nice, no complaints there. It's got its charms, I must admit.. But, and this is a big but, there have been some real disappointments. I was quite shocked, to be honest. There's this LUC tax thing, wasn't told about it upfront, and it's a hefty sum. Feels like they're hiding facts, you know? And the location, well, it's a bit far from the western expressway, makes getting around a hassle. Plus, there are some slum areas nearby, which, frankly, doesn't give you that premium feel they promised. The kitchen also felt smaller than expected. Honestly, I've had better experiences.

Okay, so Godrej Nest does have some good things going for it. I mean, getting around is pretty easy since it's got good connectivity and easy access to public transport. The location is decent too, making it easy to get to major roads. I've found it pretty convenient for commuting and running errands, which is a big plus in my book.. Man, where do I even start? First off, the customer service has been a nightmare. It felt like they were forcing me to book the property. Then, they didn't even share a draft copy of the registration! And get this a€“ if I wanted to change the floor, I'd have to pay heavy stamp duty again. Seriously? The amenities are seriously lacking, and the hall room was small. Plus, there are no balconies or dry areas in the flats, which is super inconvenient. It's situated quite inside and far away from all the accessible spaces, and the view overlooks the slums. To top it off, the pricing is way too high, and there are multiple clauses that seem disputed.

I've been living here for six years now, and I must say, the amenities are quite good for all age groups. The kids love the play areas, and the clubhouse is a nice place to unwind. I appreciate the pickup and drop service they offer; it's quite convenient. I will say that the quality of some of the work reflects the Godrej brand, but not all of it.. Honestly, there have been some disappointments. The construction quality isn't consistent; some aspects are substandard. We faced an unexpected additional cost of around 3-5 lakhs at the time of possession, which felt like being cheated. The floor tiles and washroom fittings are mediocre, and the flat sizes are somewhat compact. Having the amenities on the eth level between towers isn't ideal. The GPL RM team was quite rude and unprofessional. Also, it seems they sold flats based on an all-inclusive price but then kept adding charges. The location isn't the best either, and the pricing is very high for what you get.

Aadi Allure is one of the very few elite societies in Kanjurmarg East. It is located just besides the Eastern Express Highway. Very easily spotted from the highway and looks beautiful at night due to the lighting. There are 5 wings and one more commercial building is being made. There is a large public playground in front of the building. The air flow is really good, although it can be chilly sometimes. The internal infrastructure is very posh and high quality. Dedicated parking space (both stack and standalone) for each flat, and even guest parking outside the main gate. There is a Jain temple being constructed. There's a clubhouse which has two floors, one the top it has an event hall, rooftop lounge and dining area, and bottom has a indoor games rooms which has Carrom, Table Tennis, Pool, Foosball, Chess boards, and a fully equipped gym with a trainer. On the other side of the building, there's a small playground for children, a net practice court, and a leisure sitting area. Overall, we've had really positive experience here and also the crowd is nice. Kanjurmarg Station is just 15 mind walking or 3 mind by auto. And regarding the market facilities, there is literally everything. Vegetables, Groceries, Dairy, Stationary, Laundry, Barber, Chinese Restaurant, Non Veg Food Stalls, Wine Shop, Snacks shop et. all in the street leading to the society and most of them provide free home delivery. The society has tight security at the gates and for each wing for our safety. Society uses the MyGate ape for the management of resources and for the gate entry of visitors. There are two gates, one connecting directly to the Eastern Express Highway and other one (main) through Kanjur Village. The Kanjurmarg Police Station is very close to us, just in case. Society is fire safe and has taken care of all hazards.. There's not much to complain about the society but the surroundings might concern some people. The street outside the main gate is kinda steep so sometimes big cars and trucks have problems passing by, but they can use the Eastern Express Highway side gate to avoid that. There is a MCGM dumping ground at least a kilometer away from here, still the smell gets here sometimes, but once you start living here, it feels indifferent. The Jain Temple is still under construction and don't know how much more time the builder will take for that.

It is a gated society. No one can directly trespass without a proper security check. The children and grandparents can have a good time around walking nd playing in the garden which is just in front of the building. The society contains a club as well as a gym inbuilded for the convenience of the residents.. Inspite of the good maintenance charges sometimes the result is not well displayed. The nearby area beside the building sometime faces light problems so it becomes a issue for the residents to walk to the building in the night. The metro connectivity is currently unavailable but tho i believe when it will be available it will be very much beneficial for the society and for the residents.
